question: What physical exam finding tells you a miscarriage is threatened rather than inevitable?

options.A: Complete expulsion of the fetus
options.B: Severe lower abdominal cramping
options.C: The cervical os remains closed
options.D: Heavy and unstoppable bleeding

explanation: A closed cervix means the pregnancy tissue is still inside the uterus. This is the main sign that separates a threatened miscarriage from one that cannot be stopped. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why does vaginal bleeding happen when a pregnancy is threatened?

options.A: Partial detachment of the membrane from the uterine wall
options.B: Severe bacterial infection destroying the cervical tissues
options.C: Complete rupture of the amniotic sac inside the cavity
options.D: Rapid hormonal withdrawal causing full shedding of the lining

explanation: When the membranes pull slightly away from the inside of the uterus, tiny blood vessels tear, causing the bleeding you see on the outside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the most common reason for bleeding and loss in early pregnancy?

options.A: Chromosomal abnormalities in the fetus
options.B: Heavy physical labor by the pregnant woman
options.C: Maternal consumption of spicy foods
options.D: Acute urinary tract infections

explanation: Most first-trimester pregnancy losses happen because of natural genetic mistakes during cell division, not because of anything the mother did. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for a threatened miscarriage?

options.A: Heavy cigarette smoking habits
options.B: Regular antenatal clinic attendance
options.C: Poorly controlled endocrine conditions
options.D: Structural malformations of the uterus

explanation: Going to antenatal clinics helps protect the pregnancy and keeps both mother and baby healthy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h2)

question: What kind of tummy discomfort does a woman with a threatened miscarriage usually feel?

options.A: Absolute absence of any sensation or discomfort
options.B: Mild, dull lower abdominal aches or back pain
options.C: Sharp, stabbing pains localized to the right iliac fossa
options.D: Severe, rhythmic contractions pushing downwards

explanation: Unlike active labor, uterine activity is very low here, causing only mild aches or back pain instead of severe cramps. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h3)

question: A woman at 10 weeks has light spotting, a closed cervix, and normal vital signs. What is your best first nursing step?

options.A: Send the patient home immediately without any further evaluation
options.B: Immediately perform a surgical evacuation of the uterus in the ward
options.C: Administer high-dose oxytocin infusion to encourage quick delivery
options.D: Reassure the patient and assess vital signs while preparing for an ultrasound scan

explanation: When a patient is stable, stay calm, check her vitals, and arrange for an ultrasound to see if the baby's heart is beating. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which test tells you the most about whether the baby is okay during early bleeding?

options.A: A single routine urinalysis strip test
options.B: Pelvic ultrasonography showing cardiac activity
options.C: Abdominal girth measurement using a tape
options.D: Digital pelvic examination of the cervix

explanation: An ultrasound lets you look right at the embryo to check for a heartbeat, which is the surest sign the pregnancy is holding on. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do we check blood grouping and Rh factor for a woman with a threatened miscarriage?

options.A: To determine if an Rh-negative mother needs anti-D immunoglobulin
options.B: To measure the exact volume of blood lost during the bleeding episode
options.C: To check if the patient has a severe underlying blood infection
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: If an Rh-negative mother bleeds, her blood might mix with the baby's. Giving anti-D prevents her immune system from reacting against future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of care when a woman has a confirmed threatened miscarriage?

options.A: Immediately empty the uterine cavity using surgical instruments
options.B: Provide supportive care and monitor the progress of the pregnancy
options.C: Induce strong uterine contractions to speed up the miscarriage
options.D: Permanently suppress all natural maternal hormone production

explanation: Many of these pregnancies continue just fine. The focus is on keeping the mother comfortable and watching to see how things progress. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why don't we force strict bed rest anymore for every threatened miscarriage?

options.A: Modern evidence shows it does not prevent pregnancy loss and increases clot risks
options.B: It causes the cervix to dilate prematurely before 20 weeks
options.C: It completely stops the natural production of human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Patients refuse to stay in the hospital ward for long periods

explanation: Making a patient stay in bed doesn't stop a miscarriage, and it raises the danger of blood clots forming in her legs. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does talking kindly and counseling a woman with a threatened miscarriage help her?

options.A: It guarantees that the pregnancy will go to full term safely
options.B: It reduces her anxiety and helps her understand what to expect
options.C: It physically stops the detachment of the placenta inside the womb
options.D: It replaces the need for any form of ultrasound examination

explanation: Clear and kind words take away a lot of fear, helping the mother feel supported and informed during a stressful time. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h6)

question: A patient feels guilty, thinking her farm work caused her bleeding. What should you tell her?

options.A: Tell her to stop thinking about the pregnancy and focus on other chores
options.B: Ignore the comment because psychological feelings do not affect healing
options.C: Agree with her and scold her for engaging in strenuous physical labor
options.D: Gently reassure her that everyday activities do not cause genetic or placental issues

explanation: Clearing up misunderstandings with kindness takes away unfair self-blame and builds trust between you and the patient. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h6)

question: What dangerous condition must you always rule out when a woman has early bleeding and severe pelvic pain?

options.A: Normal twin delivery
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy can look like a normal early bleed but can cause life-threatening internal bleeding if missed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h7)

question: At a primary health clinic, when should you immediately refer a bleeding patient to a bigger hospital?

options.A: Mild fatigue reported after a routine morning walk
options.B: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads with signs of shock
options.C: Normal blood pressure and regular fetal heart sounds
options.D: A single spot of brown discharge with a closed cervix

explanation: Heavy bleeding and signs of shock mean the patient needs urgent medical help and blood transfusions that only a larger hospital can provide. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h7)

question: In which trimester does a weak cervix (cervical incompetence) usually lead to pregnancy loss?

options.A: Postpartum period
options.B: Third trimester
options.C: First trimester
options.D: Second trimester

explanation: When the cervix lacks strength, it tends to open silently between 18 and 22 weeks, which falls in the second trimester. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main sign that sets cervical incompetence apart from a threatened miscarriage?

options.A: High fever and foul-smelling discharge
options.B: Painless opening of the cervix without contractions
options.C: Severe lower tummy cramps starting weeks early
options.D: Heavy bleeding before any tissue passes

explanation: Cervical incompetence causes the cervix to open quietly without the painful uterine contractions normally seen in miscarriages or labor. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which tissue makes up the largest part of a normal, healthy cervix?

options.A: Endocrine glandular tissue
options.B: Collagen and connective tissue matrix
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Smooth muscle cells

explanation: The cervix is mainly made of fibrous tissue and collagen, giving it the strength needed to hold a pregnancy securely. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: How can past surgeries like dilation and curettage (D&C) lead to cervical incompetence?

options.A: They damage the collagen and connective tissue of the cervix
options.B: They cause strong, constant contractions of the womb
options.C: They trigger too much progesterone production early on
options.D: They permanently block the hormonal pathways of the placenta

explanation: Surgical procedures on the cervix can harm the tough collagen fibers, making it harder for the cervix to stay closed in future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h2)

question: What past pregnancy history is most typical of cervical incompetence?

options.A: Heavy bleeding after a long first stage of labor
options.B: Severe high blood pressure late in pregnancy
options.C: Repeated painless miscarriages in the second trimester
options.D: Frequent early miscarriages before 10 weeks

explanation: Losing pregnancies in the middle months without any pain or bleeding beforehand is the classic sign of a weak cervix. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks mentions she had a cone biopsy two years ago. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Reassure her that past cervical surgeries have no effect
options.B: Note it as a risk factor and arrange early ultrasound monitoring
options.C: Schedule an immediate emergency C-section
options.D: Advise her to stay on strict bed rest all pregnancy

explanation: A prior cone biopsy is a mechanical risk factor, so checking the cervical length early with an ultrasound helps keep a close, safe watch. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which scan gives the most accurate measurement of cervical length in the second trimester?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic X-ray
options.C: Manual digital examination
options.D: Routine abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Placing the ultrasound probe close to the cervix via the vagina gives a clear and precise view of its length and internal shape. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h4)

question: What does cervical 'funneling' seen on an ultrasound scan mean?

options.A: The inner opening of the cervix is opening while the outer part stays closed
options.B: The placenta is attached over the lower womb
options.C: Amniotic fluid is way above normal limits
options.D: The baby's head has dropped deep into the pelvis

explanation: Funneling happens when the upper part of the cervical canal starts to widen and form a wedge shape inside before the outer cervix opens. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h4)

question: At what gestational age is a planned cervical cerclage usually put in place?

options.A: 12 to 14 weeks
options.B: 38 to 40 weeks
options.C: 6 to 8 weeks
options.D: 28 to 30 weeks

explanation: A preventative cerclage is usually scheduled near the end of the first trimester, before the cervix has a chance to start changing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the main job of a cervical cerclage?

options.A: To prevent bacteria from traveling up into the amniotic fluid
options.B: To help dilate the birth canal early for delivery
options.C: To stop all hormone production by the ovaries
options.D: To physically support the weak cervix and keep the pregnancy secure

explanation: A cerclage acts like a purse-string stitch to give the cervix extra physical support so it stays closed under the weight of the growing baby. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which warning sign should a midwife tell a patient with a cerclage to report right away?

options.A: Mild morning sickness and food cravings
options.B: Darkening of the skin line on the belly
options.C: Gentle baby kicks felt in the abdomen
options.D: New pelvic pressure or fluid leaking

explanation: Pelvic pressure or fluid leakage can mean the stitch is failing, membranes are bulging, or labor is starting, which needs immediate medical attention. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is emotional support an important part of care for women with cervical incompetence?

options.A: Counseling takes the place of ultrasound scans
options.B: Past pregnancy losses often cause deep anxiety and fear in the current pregnancy
options.C: Stress hormones prevent the suture material from dissolving
options.D: Anxiety causes permanent damage to the muscles of the womb

explanation: Having gone through a mid-trimester loss before leaves many mothers feeling very anxious, making warm, compassionate support a key part of good midwifery care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is typical for uterine contractions when a patient has cervical incompetence?

options.A: Contractions only occur at night
options.B: Contractions are strong and frequent
options.C: Contractions are completely absent
options.D: Contractions are painful and irregular

explanation: Cervical incompetence means the cervix opens without any uterine contractions, which is why this type of loss is usually painless. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h1)

question: During which trimester do pregnancy losses most commonly happen due to cervical incompetence?

options.A: Second trimester
options.B: The very end of pregnancy
options.C: Third trimester
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby grows heavier in the second trimester, a weak cervix often gives way because it lacks the strength to stay closed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h1)

question: At what gestational age is a planned, history-based cervical stitch usually placed?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 34 to 36 weeks
options.C: 12 to 14 weeks
options.D: 8 to 10 weeks

explanation: History-based stitches are placed early in the second trimester, around 12 to 14 weeks, before the growing pregnancy puts too much weight on the cervix. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h2)

question: A patient at 20 weeks with a history of early birth has a scan showing a short cervix. What type of stitch does she receive?

options.A: Emergency rescue stitch
options.B: Postpartum repair stitch
options.C: Ultrasound-indicated
options.D: History-indicated

explanation: When a stitch is placed because an ultrasound scan shows a short cervix before 24 weeks in a high-risk woman, it is classified as ultrasound-indicated. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which surgical cerclage technique involves lifting the bladder and dissecting the tissue to place the stitch high up?

options.A: Shirodkar technique
options.B: Abdominal technique
options.C: McDonald technique
options.D: Waldmann technique

explanation: The Shirodkar method requires mucosal dissection to place the suture as high up on the cervix as possible. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is the McDonald technique often chosen over the Shirodkar method in many clinics?

options.A: It never requires local or regional anesthesia
options.B: It completely stops all uterine contractions
options.C: It is the only method that can be removed before labor
options.D: It is simpler, faster, and involves less tissue dissection

explanation: The McDonald stitch avoids mucosal dissection, making it a quicker procedure with less risk of bleeding and tissue trauma. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is a common post-operative symptom that midwives should expect after a cervical stitch procedure?

options.A: Severe continuous contractions
options.B: Mild cramping or backache
options.C: Heavy blood clots in the urine
options.D: High fever with chills

explanation: Manipulating the cervix during the stitching process frequently causes mild, temporary cramping or lower back discomfort. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which check is essential for the midwife to perform before discharging a patient who just had a cervical stitch?

options.A: Testing blood sugar levels
options.B: A complete neurological exam
options.C: Measuring pelvic bone width
options.D: Fetal heart rate auscultation

explanation: Checking the fetal heart rate confirms that the baby tolerated the procedure and anesthesia well before the mother leaves the facility. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign taught to patients after getting a cervical stitch?

options.A: Persistent lower abdominal cramping
options.B: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Leaking of watery fluid from the vagina
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and feet

explanation: Mild swelling in the legs can be normal in pregnancy, whereas foul discharge, fluid leakage, and cramping are red flags for stitch complications. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h5)

question: A patient with a McDonald stitch presents at 24 weeks with a fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge. What is the most immediate clinical priority?

options.A: Discharging her home with extra bed rest instructions
options.B: Scheduling a routine scan for four weeks later
options.C: Giving her iron supplements for mild anemia
options.D: Evaluating for infection and possible stitch removal

explanation: Fever and foul discharge point toward infection, which requires urgent evaluation and removal of the stitch to protect the mother. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h5)

question: At what gestational age is a planned cervical stitch usually removed for a normal, full-term pregnancy?

options.A: 40 to 41 weeks
options.B: 32 to 34 weeks
options.C: 36 to 37 weeks
options.D: 28 to 30 weeks

explanation: The stitch is removed around 36 to 37 weeks so the cervix can open naturally when term labor begins. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why must a cervical stitch be removed immediately if active preterm labor starts?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admission
options.B: To speed up the delivery process for the mother
options.C: To prevent the tight suture from tearing the cervical tissue
options.D: To allow the baby to grow larger before birth

explanation: If the uterus contracts and tries to push the baby out against a fixed stitch, the cervix can suffer severe tearing and laceration. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T11#BMP221_U1_T11_h6)

question: What makes an inevitable abortion different from a threatened abortion?

options.A: The cervix remains completely closed and firm to the touch.
options.B: There is never any vaginal bleeding present during the episode.
options.C: The pregnancy process cannot be stopped and will not continue.
options.D: All products of conception have already passed out of the body.

explanation: An inevitable abortion means the changes in the cervix and uterus guarantee the pregnancy will end, unlike a threatened abortion where it might survive. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is spotting an inevitable abortion early so important for a midwife?

options.A: It helps prevent heavy bleeding and reduces prolonged distress.
options.B: It ensures the woman can be discharged immediately without tests.
options.C: It allows the midwife to easily stop the process with bed rest.
options.D: It guarantees that no surgical intervention will ever be required.

explanation: Early recognition lets the midwife prepare for potential hemorrhage and manage the patient before complications worsen. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main physical difference in the cervix between a threatened and an inevitable abortion?

options.A: The cervix is always soft in threatened abortion and rigid in inevitable abortion.
options.B: The cervical os is open in inevitable abortion and closed in threatened abortion.
options.C: There are no physical differences in the cervix between the two conditions.
options.D: The cervical canal lengthens during a threatened abortion but shortens in inevitable.

explanation: A closed os means a chance of survival in threatened abortion, while an open os means the process is inevitable. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h2)

question: What happens once the internal cervical os opens during early pregnancy bleeding?

options.A: Blood flow to the placenta increases to help save the pregnancy tissue.
options.B: The cervix automatically seals itself shut to prevent any fluid loss.
options.C: The amniotic sac loses support and the pregnancy attachment breaks permanently.
options.D: The uterine muscles relax completely to let the embryo grow larger.

explanation: Opening the os removes the physical support holding the products of conception inside, leading to permanent detachment. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which symptom points most clearly to an inevitable abortion?

options.A: Cramping lower abdominal pain with a dilated cervix
options.B: High fever accompanied by a foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Painless passage of a complete, intact gestational sac
options.D: A completely closed cervix with very light spotting only

explanation: Uterine contractions cause cramping pain, which happens alongside an open cervix as the body tries to expel the tissue. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h3)

question: A woman comes to the clinic at 10 weeks pregnant with heavy bleeding and lower abdominal cramps. On examination, you see the cervical os is wide open. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Normal implantation
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy
options.C: Threatened abortion
options.D: Inevitable abortion

explanation: Heavy bleeding, cramping, and an open cervical os in early pregnancy point directly to an inevitable abortion. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a key sign to look for on an ultrasound when diagnosing an inevitable abortion?

options.A: The ovaries are enlarged with multiple large functional cysts present.
options.B: The gestational sac is seen displaced low down in the uterine cavity or cervix.
options.C: The placenta is firmly attached high up near the top of the fundus.
options.D: There are two completely normal, active twin gestational sacs visible.

explanation: Ultrasound shows the sac dropping out of its normal upper position because the attachment has failed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why does a midwife perform a speculum examination carefully during an assessment?

options.A: To manually dilate the cervix further and speed up tissue expulsion.
options.B: To visualize the cervical os and check if products of conception are descending.
options.C: To push the displaced gestational back up into the upper fundus.
options.D: To scrape the walls of the uterus clean without using any instruments.

explanation: Looking through a speculum allows the midwife to see if the os is open and if tissue is sitting in the canal. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the very first step in managing an emergency case of heavy bleeding from an inevitable abortion?

options.A: Assess airway, breathing, and circulation for stability.
options.B: Perform a detailed pelvic ultrasound scan immediately.
options.C: Administer oral iron supplements to prevent future anemia.
options.D: Send the patient home to rest until the bleeding stops.

explanation: Emergency care always starts with the primary survey checking vital life signs: airway, breathing, and circulation. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h5)

question: A patient with an inevitable abortion has a pulse of 115 beats per minute, pale skin, and heavy vaginal bleeding. What should the midwife do immediately?

options.A: Tell the patient to walk around the ward to encourage natural expulsion.
options.B: Insert a large-bore IV line and start rapid fluid resuscitation.
options.C: Prescribe mild oral analgesics and advise bed rest for two weeks.
options.D: Wait for laboratory results before taking any clinical action.

explanation: Signs of rapid pulse and paleness indicate potential shock, requiring immediate intravenous access and fluid replacement. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which medication is commonly used to help empty the uterus during an inevitable abortion?

options.A: Ergometrine tablets
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Oxytocin nasal spray
options.D: Misoprostol

explanation: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin analogue widely used to stimulate uterine contractions and empty the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is anti-D immunoglobulin given to an Rh-negative mother experiencing an inevitable abortion?

options.A: To cure any underlying bacterial infection present inside the womb.
options.B: To speed up the healing of the cervical tissues after evacuation.
options.C: To stop the heavy uterine contractions and calm the abdominal cramping.
options.D: To prevent the mother from developing antibodies against future Rh-positive babies.

explanation: Rh incompatibility can harm future pregnancies if fetal blood mixes with an Rh-negative mother, so anti-D stops sensitization. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a major long-term risk linked to untreated or infected incomplete abortions?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Permanent gestational diabetes
options.C: Tubal factor infertility
options.D: Early onset menopause

explanation: Severe pelvic infections can scar the fallopian tubes, making it difficult for future eggs to travel through them. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h7)

question: How do midwives mainly help prevent infection in a patient being treated for an inevitable abortion?

options.A: By practicing strict aseptic technique and ensuring complete uterine evacuation
options.B: By advising the patient to avoid drinking water for 24 hours post-procedure
options.C: By withholding all prescribed medications until a fever develops
options.D: By keeping the patient in a dark room with absolute bed rest for a week

explanation: Infection is prevented by keeping instruments sterile and ensuring no infected tissue remains inside the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is specialized psychological support important after an inevitable abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural beliefs often cause women to grieve silently without support.
options.B: It permanently erases all memory of the painful pregnancy loss.
options.C: Physical recovery cannot begin until emotional counseling is finished.
options.D: It is required by law before a patient can receive discharge papers.

explanation: Many women face social stigma or silence around miscarriage, making compassionate midwifery support vital for healing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h8)

question: A grieving mother is crying softly after losing her pregnancy at 10 weeks. Which action shows effective bereavement care?

options.A: Sitting quietly with her, listening patiently, and validating her feelings.
options.B: Rushing her discharge so she does not witness other pregnant women.
options.C: Minimizing the loss by explaining that early miscarriages are very common.
options.D: Telling her not to worry because she is young and can easily conceive again.

explanation: Validating emotions and providing a safe, empathetic presence helps families process their grief respectfully. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T2#BMP221_U1_T2_h8)

question: What happens in an incomplete abortion?

options.A: The embryo dies inside the uterus but the cervix stays closed
options.B: The pregnancy continues normally despite heavy bleeding
options.C: Some products of conception remain inside the uterus
options.D: All fetal and placental tissues have completely passed out

explanation: An incomplete abortion means part of the pregnancy tissue has come out, but some remains trapped inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does heavy bleeding continue when tissue stays in the uterus?

options.A: The placenta continues to produce high amounts of progesterone actively
options.B: Retained products cause a sudden drop in the woman's blood pressure
options.C: The remaining tissue stops the uterine muscle fibers from contracting tightly
options.D: Incomplete tissue loss triggers an immediate allergic reaction in the cervix

explanation: The uterus needs to contract firmly to seal off bleeding blood vessels, but trapped tissue prevents these muscles from closing properly. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the most common natural cause of early pregnancy loss?

options.A: Chromosomal abnormalities in the embryo
options.B: Excessive physical exercise by the mother
options.C: Sleeping on the back during the first trimester
options.D: Consuming too much spicy local food

explanation: Most early miscarriages happen because the embryo has genetic mistakes that prevent normal development from continuing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a cause of early pregnancy loss?

options.A: Unsafe clandestine instrumentation attempts
options.B: Severe untreated reproductive tract infections
options.C: Normal hormonal fluctuations of a healthy twin pregnancy
options.D: Uncontrolled maternal endocrine disorders

explanation: Healthy twin pregnancies experience normal hormonal shifts that support growth, rather than causing spontaneous miscarriages. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h2)

question: What exam finding strongly points to an incomplete abortion?

options.A: A thick mucous plug blocking the entire vaginal entrance
options.B: An open cervical os with active bleeding or visible tissue
options.C: A completely closed cervix with no sign of any discharge
options.D: Severe greenish-yellow foul-smelling discharge alone

explanation: When the cervix is open and blood or tissue is passing, it shows the uterus is trying to empty an incomplete pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h3)

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily with an open cervix. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Assess vital signs immediately and set up IV access for fluid replacement
options.B: Send the patient home to rest until the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform a detailed dietary history to check for iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Counsel the woman on future family planning methods before treatment

explanation: Heavy bleeding and dizziness indicate potential shock, making immediate vital sign checks and intravenous line placement the top priority. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h3)

question: How can you tell a threatened abortion apart from an incomplete abortion?

options.A: Bleeding is always absent in a threatened abortion but heavy in an incomplete abortion
options.B: The cervical os is closed in a threatened abortion and open in an incomplete abortion
options.C: Abdominal pain never occurs in women experiencing a threatened abortion
options.D: The uterus feels much larger in a threatened abortion than in an incomplete one

explanation: The status of the cervix is the key physical difference: closed means the pregnancy might continue, while open with tissue passage means it is incomplete. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which condition features grape-like tissue vesicles and a uterus larger than expected?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Incomplete abortion
options.C: Molar pregnancy
options.D: Cervical polyp

explanation: A molar pregnancy involves abnormal tissue growth that creates characteristic grape-like clusters and rapid uterine enlargement. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are uterotonic drugs given during an incomplete abortion?

options.A: To relax the abdominal muscles and relieve severe cramping pain
options.B: To stop secondary bacterial infections from entering the uterus
options.C: To stimulate uterine contractions and reduce ongoing blood loss
options.D: To permanently prevent future pregnancies from implanting

explanation: Uterotonics make the uterine muscle fibers clamp down tightly on open blood vessels, slowing down heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason for securing a large IV line in a woman with an incomplete abortion?

options.A: To provide long-term intravenous nutrition during recovery
options.B: To collect continuous hourly urine output samples easily
options.C: To inject local anesthesia directly into the systemic circulation
options.D: To allow rapid fluid resuscitation and administer emergency medications

explanation: Large IV lines allow quick delivery of fluids to combat shock and fast administration of life-saving drugs when bleeding is severe. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) used for?

options.A: Measuring the exact hormone levels circulating in the placenta
options.B: Gently emptying the retained products of conception from the uterus
options.C: Injecting antibiotics directly into the bloodstream to clear sepsis
options.D: Dilating the cervix permanently to prevent future pregnancies

explanation: MVA uses a specialized suction device to safely and quickly clear out any remaining pregnancy tissue from the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h6)

question: When is medical management with misoprostol chosen over surgery?

options.A: When the patient is actively bleeding to the point of hypovolemic shock
options.B: When the patient prefers to avoid surgery and the clinical condition is stable
options.C: When the gestational age is past the second trimester limit
options.D: When there is an established, severe intrauterine infection present

explanation: Medical management offers a non-surgical alternative favored by many stable patients, provided there is no emergency bleeding or severe infection. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h6)

question: How soon can a woman become fertile again after an incomplete abortion?

options.A: Within two weeks
options.B: After six months
options.C: After three full cycles
options.D: Only after one year

explanation: Ovulation can return as early as two weeks after an abortion, meaning a woman can get pregnant again before her next period. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h7)

question: A patient recovering from an evacuation wants to delay her next pregnancy. When should family planning counseling happen?

options.A: Before discharge, so she can start a chosen method immediately
options.B: Only after she has completed three normal menstrual periods
options.C: Advise her to avoid all discussions about sex for at least one year
options.D: Wait until her six-week postnatal checkup to avoid overwhelming her

explanation: Because fertility returns rapidly, counseling and contraception should happen before the patient leaves the health facility. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is a long-term complication caused by scar tissue inside the uterus from aggressive curettage?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Asherman's syndrome
options.C: Chronic cervical incompetence
options.D: Gestational trophoblastic disease

explanation: Asherman's syndrome involves scar tissue forming inside the uterine cavity, which can cause painful periods and secondary infertility. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h8)

question: Which signs suggest that an incomplete abortion has progressed to a septic abortion?

options.A: A completely closed cervix with no vaginal bleeding
options.B: High fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Slow pulse rate and low blood pressure alone
options.D: Mild cramping pain without any systemic symptoms

explanation: Fever, chills, and foul-smelling discharge are classic signs that retained tissue has become infected, leading to sepsis. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h8)

question: What defines a complete abortion in early pregnancy?

options.A: The cervix opens wide without any tissue passing out
options.B: All products of conception are totally expelled from the uterus
options.C: The fetus is expelled but the placenta remains inside
options.D: Bleeding stops temporarily but the pregnancy continues

explanation: A complete abortion means everything, including the fetus, membranes, and placenta, has left the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does bleeding typically stop or slow down significantly after a complete abortion?

options.A: Clotting factors instantly multiply across the entire body
options.B: Low blood pressure naturally forces the bleeding to dry up
options.C: Strong uterine contractions close off the open blood vessels
options.D: The patient drinks large amounts of cold water to cool down

explanation: When the uterus is completely empty, it contracts firmly, which squeezes the open blood vessels shut to stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the typical state of the external cervical os during a speculum examination for a complete abortion?

options.A: Bulging
options.B: Closed
options.C: Rigid
options.D: Wide open

explanation: Once all pregnancy tissue has passed and the uterus contracts, the cervix closes back up. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic stating she passed a fleshy mass an hour ago, and her severe lower abdominal cramps have now stopped completely. What is the most likely initial assessment finding?

options.A: An open cervical os with active heavy bleeding
options.B: A rigid, severely tender abdomen with high fever
options.C: A greatly enlarged uterus with fetal parts felt
options.D: A closed cervix and a uterus smaller than expected

explanation: Passing the tissue means the abortion is likely complete, resulting in a closed cervix and a smaller, contracted uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which condition features persistent bleeding and cramping with an open cervical os, unlike a complete abortion?

options.A: Normal menstruation
options.B: Incomplete abortion
options.C: Implantation spotting
options.D: Completed miscarriage

explanation: An incomplete abortion still has tissue inside the uterus, so the cervix stays open and bleeding continues. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is NOT a common differential diagnosis for bleeding in early pregnancy?

options.A: Term labor
options.B: Molar pregnancy
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Threatened abortion

explanation: Term labor happens at the end of a full pregnancy, not in early pregnancy when bleeding first occurs. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary ultrasound finding that confirms a complete abortion?

options.A: Multiple grape-like clusters filling the whole uterus
options.B: An empty uterine cavity with a thin endometrial lining
options.C: A gestational sac containing a live, active fetal heart
options.D: A thick mass of retained placental tissue and blood clots

explanation: An ultrasound showing an empty uterus with a thin lining proves that all products of conception have been expelled. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is a transvaginal ultrasound preferred over a general abdominal scan when checking for complete abortion?

options.A: It is completely painless and avoids touching the vaginal area
options.B: It gives a much clearer, closer view of the empty uterine cavity
options.C: It costs nothing for the patient to perform in rural clinics
options.D: It requires the patient to drink large amounts of water first

explanation: Transvaginal probes sit closer to the uterus, allowing midwives and doctors to clearly see if any tissue remains inside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient has a confirmed complete abortion on ultrasound with minimal spotting and stable vital signs. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.A: Perform a repeat manual vacuum aspiration to clean the lining
options.B: Rush the patient to the theater for immediate surgical evacuation
options.C: Provide supportive care, reassurance, and discharge instructions
options.D: Start high-dose intravenous antibiotics and admit for two weeks

explanation: Because the uterus is already empty, surgery is unnecessary, and the patient only needs support and recovery advice. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h5)

question: When are prophylactic antibiotics typically recommended for a patient with a complete abortion?

options.A: Only when the patient requests pain relief medications
options.B: Never under any circumstances in maternity care settings
options.C: Only if there are signs of infection such as fever or foul discharge
options.D: For every single patient regardless of their physical examination

explanation: Routine antibiotics are not needed for a clean, complete abortion unless infection is clinically suspected. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is immediate contraceptive counseling important following a complete abortion?

options.A: Fertility can return as early as two weeks after the event
options.B: Hormonal contraceptives instantly cure uterine infections
options.C: Women are legally required to wait two years before conceiving
options.D: Pregnancy is biologically impossible for a full year afterward

explanation: Ovulation can resume very quickly after a miscarriage, so patients need birth control guidance right away if they wish to avoid immediate pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is an important part of holistic post-abortion care besides physical healing?

options.A: Strict bed rest at home for at least one full month
options.B: Isolating the patient from family members to ensure rest
options.C: Providing compassionate emotional support and grief counseling
options.D: Mandatory referral to a psychiatric hospital for strong sedatives

explanation: Emotional support helps patients process the loss and ensures they receive holistic, empathetic care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h6)

question: What primary condition defines a septic abortion?

options.A: Normal pregnancy associated with a high fever
options.B: Complete expulsion of the products of conception
options.C: Bleeding after twenty weeks of gestation
options.D: Miscarriage complicated by intrauterine infection

explanation: A septic abortion specifically refers to any miscarriage or abortion that has become infected inside the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do retained products of conception increase the risk of severe infection?

options.A: They block the normal flow of urine from the bladder
options.B: They stop the production of progesterone hormones
options.C: They act as a growth medium for bacteria to multiply
options.D: They cause an immediate drop in maternal blood pressure

explanation: Dead tissue left inside the uterus provides rich nutrients where invading bacteria can easily multiply and spread. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following organisms is a common gram-negative cause of septic abortion originating from the bowel?

options.A: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Clostridium tetani

explanation: Escherichia coli is a normal gut bacterium that frequently contaminates the genital tract and causes severe uterine infections. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h2)

question: A young woman presents with a severe septic abortion after visiting an uncertified herbalist. What primary factor likely contributed to her condition?

options.A: Use of unsterile instruments during an unsafe procedure
options.B: Consuming too many spicy foods during early pregnancy
options.C: Failure to take routine prenatal multivitamin supplements
options.D: Engaging in heavy physical labor while carrying twins

explanation: Unsafe procedures performed by unskilled providers using unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria directly into the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which symptom strongly points to a localized uterine infection in early pregnancy loss?

options.A: Sudden loss of the sense of taste
options.B: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Painless swelling of both ankles
options.D: Itchy skin rashes on the abdomen

explanation: A foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge is a classic sign of bacterial growth and tissue breakdown inside the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h3)

question: What indicates that a septic abortion has progressed from Stage 1 to Stage 2?

options.A: The fetus has been delivered completely alive and healthy
options.B: The patient's blood pressure has returned completely to normal
options.C: The bleeding has stopped without any medical intervention
options.D: The infection has spread beyond the uterus into pelvic tissues

explanation: Stage 2 represents the extension of the infection outside the uterine walls into the surrounding pelvic structures and peritoneum. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why must intravenous fluid resuscitation begin before taking a patient with septic shock to the operating theatre?

options.A: To dilute the concentration of antibiotics in the bloodstream
options.B: To ensure the patient remains fully awake during the procedure
options.C: To restore blood pressure and protect vital organ perfusion
options.D: To completely stop all uterine bleeding without surgery

explanation: Restoring circulating blood volume stabilizes the patient and prevents kidney failure or shock collapse during anesthesia. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which clinical action should be performed immediately after drawing blood cultures in a septic patient?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with oral medications
options.B: Administering broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Waiting forty-eight hours for laboratory results
options.D: Performing an immediate diagnostic ultrasound scan

explanation: Prompt administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics is vital to control spreading infection and prevent septic shock. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is surgical evacuation necessary alongside antibiotic therapy in septic abortion?

options.A: Surgery helps the patient produce more red blood cells
options.B: Antibiotics cannot enter the bloodstream of a pregnant woman
options.C: Infected retained tissue keeps the infection active
options.D: Curettage removes the need to monitor urine output

explanation: Antibiotics alone cannot clear the infection if dead, infected placental or fetal tissue remains inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h5)

question: What major surgical risk is heightened when evacuating a septic and inflamed uterus?

options.A: Hypertensive crisis
options.B: Complete bone fracture
options.C: Uterine perforation
options.D: Obstructed labor

explanation: An infected myometrium is soft and friable, making accidental perforation by surgical instruments much easier. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary underlying cause of acute renal failure in severe septic abortion?

options.A: A complete blockage of the urethra by a blood clot
options.B: Eating contaminated foods while admitted to the ward
options.C: Prolonged low blood pressure leading to poor kidney perfusion
options.D: Taking too many oral painkillers before coming to the hospital

explanation: Septic shock lowers blood pressure drastically, starving the kidneys of oxygen and blood flow, which causes tubular damage. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which complication involves a widespread disturbance of the blood-clotting system?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Disseminated intravascular coagulation

explanation: DIC is a serious systemic condition where clotting factors are consumed rapidly, causing simultaneous bleeding and clotting. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is contraceptive counseling an essential part of post-abortion care?

options.A: It is required by law before the patient can leave the hospital
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never experience infections again
options.C: It helps prevent repeat unwanted pregnancies and unsafe procedures
options.D: It stops the uterus from contracting after surgical evacuation

explanation: Providing accessible contraception protects women from falling into the cycle of recurrent unsafe abortions and sepsis. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h7)

question: What approach should midwives use when counseling a patient recovering from a septic abortion?

options.A: Strict scolding to prevent future mistakes
options.B: Ignoring the incident to avoid emotional stress
options.C: Involving local law enforcement immediately
options.D: Empathetic and non-judgmental communication

explanation: Patients recovering from clandestine procedures need compassionate, non-judgmental support to encourage trust and health-seeking behavior. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the main feature of a missed abortion?

options.A: Severe heavy bleeding starts suddenly before any pain begins
options.B: Active uterine contractions push out the pregnancy immediately
options.C: The pregnancy tissue stops growing inside the uterus but is not expelled
options.D: The placenta delivers normally while the fetus remains alive

explanation: In a missed abortion, the fetus has stopped developing or died, but the cervix stays closed, so the tissue stays inside the uterus instead of coming out right away. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do many patients with a missed abortion not realize right away that something is wrong?

options.A: They develop a high fever that masks all other pregnancy symptoms
options.B: They lack the typical warning signs like heavy bleeding and severe pain
options.C: They experience intense uterine contractions that feel like normal labor
options.D: Their blood pressure drops dangerously low within the first few hours

explanation: Because the cervix stays closed and the tissue is kept inside without causing immediate pain or bleeding, many women do not have obvious physical signs of the loss. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the most common reason for early pregnancy losses like a missed abortion?

options.A: Eating excessive amounts of spicy local Nigerian foods
options.B: Failure of the mother to take routine malaria prophylaxis
options.C: Heavy physical labor during the early weeks of gestation
options.D: Chromosomal abnormalities within the developing embryo

explanation: Most early miscarriages happen because of natural genetic or chromosomal errors in the growing embryo, not because of anything the mother did or ate. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h2)

question: How does the physical process of a missed abortion happen in the body?

options.A: Infection builds up immediately and creates a solid pelvic mass
options.B: Strong muscular spasms open the cervix wide within minutes
options.C: The placenta instantly grows larger to push out the dead tissue
options.D: Hormone levels drop and tissue detaches, but the cervix stays closed

explanation: When a pregnancy stops growing, hormone levels fall and the sac detaches from the uterine wall. However, if the cervix fails to open, the tissue stays trapped inside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h2)

question: During a physical check, which finding points strongly toward a missed abortion?

options.A: A loud fetal heart sound is heard through a stethoscope
options.B: The cervix is fully dilated with active tissue extrusion
options.C: Uterine size is smaller than expected for gestational dates
options.D: Blood pressure is dangerously elevated above normal limits

explanation: Because growth has stopped and some tissue is slowly absorbed or fluids decrease, the uterus often feels smaller than it should be for the patient's expected weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h3)

question: What do women often notice happening to their early pregnancy signs right before a missed abortion is found?

options.A: Their breast tenderness and morning sickness stopped quite suddenly
options.B: They began passing large clots of bright red blood every morning
options.C: They experienced intense, sharp pains centered in the lower back
options.D: Their appetite increased dramatically over a period of three days

explanation: As pregnancy hormone levels drop after the fetus stops growing, normal early signs like nausea and sore breasts tend to fade away fast. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which test gives a clear, definite confirmation of a missed abortion?

options.A: A single routine urinalysis test for sugar and protein
options.B: Manual abdominal palpation to check for maternal reflexes
options.C: Measuring the mother's daily body temperature using a thermometer
options.D: Pelvic ultrasonography showing no embryonic cardiac activity

explanation: An ultrasound scan is the best way to confirm the diagnosis by showing a pregnancy sac without a heartbeat. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is checking the hemoglobin level important before treating a missed abortion?

options.A: It measures the exact hormonal output of the failing placenta
options.B: It proves whether the patient has an active bacterial infection
options.C: Baseline anemia is common, and treatment may involve blood loss
options.D: High hemoglobin levels completely prevent the need for any surgery

explanation: Many women already have low blood counts due to nutritional anemia, so it is vital to check hemoglobin before any procedure that might cause bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which medication is commonly used to help the uterus pass the tissue in a missed abortion?

options.A: Ergometrine
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Misoprostol is a medication that helps soften the cervix and gently stimulates the uterus to contract and clear out the remaining tissue. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) often chosen instead of sharp metal curettage?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any form of local or general pain relief
options.B: It works instantly without causing any uterine contractions or cramping
options.C: It has a lower risk of uterine perforation and fewer overall complications
options.D: It forces the placenta to reattach and allows the pregnancy to continue

explanation: MVA uses a soft plastic tube and gentle suction, which is much safer and less likely to damage the wall of the uterus compared to sharp metal instruments. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h5)

question: What are the main signs that a miscarriage has become infected?

options.A: Total absence of pain combined with excessive hunger
options.B: High blood pressure and severe throbbing headaches
options.C: Fever, pelvic pain, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: Sudden weight gain and swelling in both lower legs

explanation: An infection inside the uterus usually causes a high temperature, lower tummy pain, and bad-smelling vaginal discharge. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h6)

question: A patient with a missed abortion has heavy bleeding and a fast pulse of 120 beats per minute. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to walk around the ward to encourage tissue passage
options.B: Start intravenous fluid resuscitation and summon medical help urgently
options.C: Wait for laboratory blood test results before taking any clinical steps
options.D: Discharge the patient home with oral analgesics and a follow-up date

explanation: A fast pulse and heavy bleeding are signs of shock from blood loss. Starting IV fluids right away and calling for senior help is a life-saving priority. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h6)

question: How should a midwife care for the emotional needs of a woman experiencing a missed abortion?

options.A: Blame lifestyle choices to prevent future pregnancy losses
options.B: Focus strictly on physical procedures and avoid discussing feelings
options.C: Provide compassionate counseling and validate her feelings of grief
options.D: Advise her to forget the loss quickly because it was very early

explanation: A miscarriage is a real loss. Listening with empathy and validating the parents' grief helps support their emotional healing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is it important for midwives to talk about cultural myths regarding miscarriage during counseling?

options.A: To ensure the family pays all hospital bills promptly before leaving
options.B: To prove that modern medical science has answers for every single event
options.C: To convince the patient to undergo immediate major abdominal surgery
options.D: To relieve unnecessary guilt and self-blame experienced by the mother

explanation: Many women carry unfair guilt because of community myths about what caused the loss. Explaining the true medical facts helps take away that heavy emotional burden. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h7)

question: Where do the vast majority of ectopic pregnancies implant?

options.A: Fallopian tube
options.B: Cervical canal
options.C: Ovary surface
options.D: Abdominal cavity

explanation: The fallopian tube is the most common site for abnormal implantation because transport of the fertilized egg can be delayed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why does a tubal pregnancy frequently lead to tissue rupture?

options.A: The embryo grows too slowly to trigger normal hormones.
options.B: High uterine contractions push the tissue backward.
options.C: Excessive mucus production blocks the tube completely.
options.D: The tubal wall is thin and lacks a protective submucosa.

explanation: Because the fallopian tube cannot stretch or support a growing pregnancy like the uterus, it tears as the trophoblast invades. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which condition is a major infectious cause of tubal damage leading to ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

explanation: Infections that cause pelvic inflammatory disease leave scar tissue inside the fallopian tubes, which can trap a fertilized egg. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h2)

question: A patient presents with early pregnancy symptoms and a history of untreated chlamydia infection. Why does this history raise your suspicion?

options.A: Chlamydia stops the ovaries from producing progesterone entirely.
options.B: Chlamydia causes the uterus to shrink in size.
options.C: Chlamydia thickens the cervical mucus to trap all sperm.
options.D: Chlamydia damages the delicate cilia needed to move the egg to the uterus.

explanation: Infections create scar tissue and destroy the tiny hair-like structures inside the tube that push the blastocyst forward. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which section of the fallopian tube houses most ectopic implantations?

options.A: Interstitial segment
options.B: Fimbriae
options.C: Isthmus
options.D: Ampulla

explanation: The ampulla is the widest and longest section of the fallopian tube, making it the most frequent spot for an embryo to lodge. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is an interstitial ectopic pregnancy considered particularly dangerous?

options.A: It always resolves spontaneously without causing any symptoms.
options.B: It prevents the placenta from forming at all.
options.C: It grows inside the ovary rather than the fallopian tube.
options.D: It involves a region with a very rich blood supply near the uterus.

explanation: Because the interstitial portion sits in the muscular wall of the uterus near major vessels, rupture leads to sudden, catastrophic bleeding. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h3)

question: What causes shoulder tip pain in a patient with a suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Blood in the abdominal cavity irritating the diaphragm
options.B: A secondary bone infection in the shoulder joint
options.C: Severe muscle strain from vomiting
options.D: Nerve compression from high blood pressure

explanation: Internal bleeding pools in the abdomen and irritates the phrenic nerve, which refers pain upward to the shoulder area. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h4)

question: A young woman comes to the clinic feeling dizzy and faint, with sharp right-sided pelvic pain after missing one period. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Provide oral contraceptive pills to regulate her menstrual cycle
options.B: Schedule a routine antenatal booking visit for the following month
options.C: Assess for signs of internal bleeding and prepare for emergency medical response
options.D: Send her home with pain relievers and tell her to return next week

explanation: These symptoms strongly suggest a ruptured ectopic pregnancy with internal bleeding, which requires urgent emergency care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which imaging tool provides the best view for diagnosing an early ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Routine magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.C: Plain abdominal X-ray
options.D: Standard pelvic CT scan

explanation: Transvaginal ultrasound gives a clear view of the uterine cavity and surrounding areas, helping to spot an extra-uterine pregnancy early. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is a urine pregnancy test alone insufficient to confirm a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It only works after the twentieth week of gestation.
options.B: It confirms the presence of human chorionic gonadotropin but cannot show where the pregnancy is implanted.
options.C: It cannot detect twin pregnancies or molar conditions.
options.D: It turns negative immediately if the patient feels any abdominal pain.

explanation: A positive test only proves that hCG is present in the body, meaning the pregnancy could be inside or outside the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary emergency nursing action when a patient collapses from a suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around to improve circulation.
options.B: Establish large-bore intravenous access and prepare for fluid resuscitation.
options.C: Apply a tight abdominal binder to stop internal bleeding.
options.D: Administer oral rehydration salts and wait for natural recovery.

explanation: Rapid vascular access is vital to replace lost fluids and blood volume during shock caused by internal hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is cross-matching blood urgently required during a tubal rupture emergency?

options.A: Laboratory regulations require blood samples for all emergency admissions.
options.B: Blood tests help confirm the exact gestational age of the fetus.
options.C: It prevents the body from rejecting intravenous saline solutions.
options.D: Massive internal bleeding requires rapid blood replacement during surgery.

explanation: A ruptured tube spills large amounts of blood into the peritoneal cavity, making prompt transfusion essential to prevent death. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of methotrexate in treating an unruptured ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: It stimulates the immune system to attack bacterial infections.
options.B: It causes immediate contraction of the uterine muscle walls.
options.C: It dissolves blood clots inside the peritoneal cavity.
options.D: It blocks folic acid to stop rapid cell division in the trophoblast.

explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate metabolism, causing the rapidly dividing cells of the pregnancy to stop growing and eventually reabsorb. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h7)

question: When would a surgeon choose to perform a salpingectomy rather than a salpingostomy?

options.A: When the patient is young and desperately wants to have more children.
options.B: When the fallopian tube is severely damaged and bleeding cannot be controlled.
options.C: When the patient refuses all forms of general anesthesia.
options.D: When the gestational sac is located inside the normal uterine cavity.

explanation: If the tube is badly ruptured or compromised, removing it completely is safer to prevent persistent ectopic tissue or recurrent hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why do healthcare providers advise waiting a while before trying for another pregnancy after methotrexate treatment?

options.A: To guarantee that the menstrual cycle stops permanently
options.B: To allow the ovaries time to produce double the normal number of eggs
options.C: To ensure the drug is fully cleared and prevent potential harmful effects on a new pregnancy
options.D: To strengthen the abdominal muscles after surgical incisions

explanation: Methotrexate can harm early fetal development, so the body needs time to eliminate the medication completely before a new conception. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h8)

question: A patient who lost her fallopian tube from an ectopic pregnancy expresses deep fear that she will never have a baby. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Advise her to adopt a child immediately because her reproductive life has ended.
options.B: Tell her that losing one tube makes natural conception completely impossible forever.
options.C: Encourage her to ignore the loss and focus entirely on her current work.
options.D: Reassure her that pregnancy is still possible with the remaining healthy tube, and discuss early screening for next time.

explanation: Empathetic counselling provides factual reassurance about the function of the remaining tube and outlines proactive steps for future care. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T7#BMP221_U1_T7_h8)

question: What is another name commonly used for a hydatidiform mole in clinical practice?

options.A: Molar pregnancy
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Missed miscarriage
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Hydatidiform mole is widely referred to as a molar pregnancy because the abnormal mass resembles a mole or cluster of grapes inside the uterus. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is it important for midwives to monitor gestational trophoblastic diseases closely during early pregnancy?

options.A: They prevent the woman from ever producing normal eggs in the future
options.B: They can sometimes develop into cancerous conditions if not properly monitored
options.C: They always cause immediate maternal death in the first trimester
options.D: They automatically cause severe bone infections throughout the pelvis

explanation: Although most moles are benign, abnormal trophoblastic tissue can turn into gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, requiring careful follow-up. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which type of molar pregnancy contains no fetal or embryonic tissue at all?

options.A: Invasive mole
options.B: Partial mole
options.C: Choriocarcinoma
options.D: Complete mole

explanation: A complete mole forms entirely from paternal genetic material, completely lacking any fetal parts or embryonic structures. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h2)

question: What genetic feature is typical of a partial hydatidiform mole?

options.A: An extra set of chromosomes caused by fertilization with multiple sperm
options.B: Complete absence of any nuclear DNA inside the egg
options.C: Purely paternal chromosomes with duplicated material
options.D: Normal maternal chromosomes paired with no sperm

explanation: Partial moles typically arise when two sperm fertilize a single normal egg, yielding a triploid set of chromosomes. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical sign or symptom of a molar pregnancy?

options.A: Passage of tissue vesicles resembling grapes
options.B: Uterine size much larger than expected for dates
options.C: Fetal kicking felt clearly at 10 weeks
options.D: Severe and persistent nausea and vomiting

explanation: Fetal movements cannot be felt at 10 weeks, especially in a molar pregnancy where normal fetal development is absent or severely compromised. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h3)

question: A 22-year-old woman presents at 12 weeks with severe vomiting, vaginal bleeding, and a uterus measuring the size of an 18-week pregnancy. What condition should the midwife suspect first?

options.A: Ectopic implantation
options.B: Hydatidiform mole
options.C: Normal twin pregnancy
options.D: Incomplete miscarriage

explanation: The classic triad of bleeding, excessive uterine size for dates, and severe hyperemesis strongly points toward a molar pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h3)

question: What descriptive term do sonographers use for a complete molar pregnancy on an ultrasound scan?

options.A: Mickey mouse sign
options.B: Snowstorm appearance
options.C: Lemon sign
options.D: Double decidual sac

explanation: The numerous small cystic spaces inside a complete mole create a characteristic snowstorm or speckled echo pattern on ultrasound scans. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why is measuring blood human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) crucial in managing molar pregnancies?

options.A: Low hormone levels confirm that a complete mole is present
options.B: It measures the exact amount of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus
options.C: Molar tissue produces extremely high amounts of this hormone
options.D: It tells the clinician whether the patient has a bacterial infection

explanation: Because molar tissue consists of proliferating trophoblasts, serum hCG levels rise much higher than in normal pregnancies. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the preferred method for evacuating a hydatidiform mole from the uterus?

options.A: Suction curettage
options.B: Medical induction with misoprostol alone
options.C: Immediate total abdominal hysterectomy
options.D: Sharp metal curettage without suction

explanation: Vacuum aspiration or suction curettage is the safest and most effective method for removing molar tissue while minimizing uterine trauma. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why should oxytocin infusion be delayed until suction evacuation has started in molar pregnancies?

options.A: To stop the blood hCG levels from dropping too quickly
options.B: To allow the cervix enough time to close tightly around instruments
options.C: To ensure the patient experiences maximum pain relief during the procedure
options.D: To prevent forcing molar tissue into the maternal blood vessels

explanation: Contracting the uterus prematurely before evacuation begins can drive tumor emboli into the maternal circulation, leading to severe pulmonary complications. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is reliable contraception strongly advised during the post-evacuation follow-up period?

options.A: Contraceptive pills destroy any remaining cancer cells in the ovaries
options.B: Hormonal contraceptives prevent the woman from ever ovulating again
options.C: A new pregnancy makes it hard to track hCG levels for remaining disease
options.D: The uterus is permanently damaged and cannot hold another baby

explanation: A fresh pregnancy naturally raises hCG levels, which confuses clinicians trying to monitor whether the molar tissue has fully resolved or turned malignant. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h6)

question: How often should blood hCG levels be checked immediately after a molar evacuation?

options.A: Every six months until the next menstrual period
options.B: Only once after a full year has passed
options.C: Daily while the patient is admitted on the ward
options.D: Weekly until normal for three consecutive weeks

explanation: Weekly testing ensures that any plateau or rise in hCG is caught immediately, signaling the need for further medical intervention. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T8#BMP221_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which type of prior pregnancy is most often linked to the development of choriocarcinoma?

options.A: Preterm vaginal birth
options.B: Normal term delivery
options.C: Unruptured ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Hydatidiform mole

explanation: About half of all choriocarcinoma cases develop after a molar pregnancy, which is why careful follow-up of moles is so important. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h1)

question: How do choriocarcinoma cells usually spread to distant organs in the body?

options.A: Across the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Directly through the fallopian tubes
options.C: Via the lymphatic system
options.D: Through the bloodstream

explanation: These tumor cells tend to invade local blood vessels early, allowing them to travel through the blood to organs like the lungs. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common sign of choriocarcinoma within the reproductive tract?

options.A: Complete cervical stenosis
options.B: Uterine subinvolution
options.C: Hypertrophied ovarian cysts
options.D: Atrophic vaginal mucosa

explanation: Because the tumor continues to grow inside the muscular wall of the uterus, the organ fails to shrink back to its normal size after a pregnancy loss or delivery. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h2)

question: A patient returns six weeks after a molar evacuation complaining of a persistent cough and blood-streaked sputum. What complication should the midwife suspect?

options.A: Primary lung infection
options.B: Pulmonary metastasis
options.C: Normal postpartum rhinitis
options.D: Severe bronchial asthma

explanation: The lungs are the most common site for distant spread, and respiratory symptoms following a molar pregnancy require immediate checks for metastasis. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which laboratory marker is primarily monitored to diagnose and follow up suspected choriocarcinoma?

options.A: Alpha-fetoprotein
options.B: Cancer antigen 125
options.C: Lactate dehydrogenase
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: The cells produce large amounts of hCG, making serial blood tests of this hormone the main way to track disease activity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why is a chest X-ray routinely ordered during the workup for suspected choriocarcinoma?

options.A: To check for common lung metastases
options.B: To rule out primary pneumonia
options.C: To measure baseline respiratory rate
options.D: To assess cardiac output before surgery

explanation: Choriocarcinoma spreads early through the bloodstream, and the lungs are the most frequent secondary site to check. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary treatment used for managing choriocarcinoma?

options.A: Radiation therapy
options.B: Radical hysterectomy
options.C: Hormone replacement
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: These tumors respond very well to anti-cancer drugs, making medication the main cure strategy even when the cancer has spread. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h4)

question: When is a hysterectomy most commonly considered in a patient with choriocarcinoma?

options.A: To replace the need for chemotherapy
options.B: To control severe uterine bleeding
options.C: When the patient desires future pregnancy
options.D: As the first-line cure for all stages

explanation: Surgery is rarely the main cure, but it is used to stop dangerous bleeding from the tumor or when the disease does not respond to medication in patients who are done having children. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the recommended time to wait before trying to get pregnant again after completing treatment for choriocarcinoma?

options.A: Only three months
options.B: Exactly five years
options.C: No waiting period is needed
options.D: At least one year

explanation: Delaying pregnancy for twelve months allows healthcare providers to monitor hCG levels accurately without confusion from a new gestation. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h5)

question: A patient treated for choriocarcinoma asks why she must use reliable contraception. What is the best explanation?

options.A: Her uterus is permanently damaged and cannot hold a pregnancy safely.
options.B: A new pregnancy would make it hard to track hCG hormone levels for cancer recurrence.
options.C: Her body requires absolute rest to rebuild normal blood volume.
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs remain active in her breast milk for several years.

explanation: A normal pregnancy also produces hCG, so conceiving too soon would hide whether rising hormone levels mean the cancer has returned. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h5)

question: At how many weeks of pregnancy does bleeding from the birth canal officially count as antepartum haemorrhage (APH)?

options.A: Twenty-two completed weeks of pregnancy
options.B: Sixteen completed weeks of pregnancy
options.C: Thirty-six completed weeks of pregnancy
options.D: Ten completed weeks of pregnancy

explanation: APH is defined as bleeding from the genital tract from the 22nd week of pregnancy until the baby is born. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is a normal bloody "show" not considered antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Because a show involves a much larger volume of blood loss than an APH
options.B: Because a show always occurs before the twentieth week of pregnancy
options.C: Because a show originates entirely from maternal urinary tract infections
options.D: Because a show is a normal sign of impending labour rather than a pathological event

explanation: A show is the normal passing of mucus tinged with a little blood when the cervix opens for birth, whereas APH is a pregnancy complication. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h1)

question: What are the two most common major causes of antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Chronic hypertension and gestational diabetes
options.B: Vasa praevia and marginal sinus bleeding
options.C: Uterine rupture and cervical polyps
options.D: Placenta praevia and placental abruption

explanation: Placenta praevia and placental abruption are responsible for most episodes of heavy bleeding in the second half of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h2)
